papers.title: Postselection on Halting and Reductions to the Halting Problem
papers.abstract: A probabilistic Turing machine is an ordinary Turing machine that may also toss fair coins, with no limit on its running time or memory. If it always halts, it decides only computable problems. Aaronson et al. studied machines that may run forever on some coin tosses, with the answer read only from the runs that halt. Suppose the correct answer must be more than twice as likely as the wrong one. They showed that these machines decide exactly the problems solvable with a fixed list of questions about the halting problem. They asked what happens when the correct answer need only be the more likely one. We show that the machines then decide exactly the problems solvable by asking such questions one after another, each chosen after the earlier answers. We also show that the factor two can be replaced by any fixed factor greater than one. A machine may promise two numbers: a lower bound on its probability of halting, and a lower bound on its probability of being right when it halts. From these two numbers we compute exactly how many questions fixed in advance the machine can replace. The main idea is that probability acts as a budget for how often a computable guess may change its mind. The results extend to oracle machines and to machines nested inside each other. Quantum machines decide the same problems.

papers.title: On homogeneous hypertournaments
papers.abstract: Sullivan recently constructed continuum many countable homogeneous $n$-hypertournaments for every $n\ge3$ by forbidding configurations he calls pair-cancelling. We show that, for every family $\mathcal F$ of pair-cancelling $n$-hypertournaments, the class of all linearly ordered finite $\mathcal F$-free $n$-hypertournaments is Ramsey and has the ordering property. In particular, freely ordered $\mathbf{H}_4$-free $3$-hypertournaments are Ramsey, answering a question of Cherlin, Hubi\v{c}ka, Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il, and the author from 2021. For every odd $n\ge3$, we give a simple Ramsey expansion with the expansion property for even $n$-hypertournaments by naming an $(n-1)$-hypertournament and a free linear order. We also show that, for $n\ge6$, no unbounded hereditary strong amalgamation class of finite $n$-hypertournaments has EPPA. Moreover, we prove the failure of EPPA for all Sullivan's classes with $n\ge4$, and for the even $5$-hypertournaments. We conjecture that even hypertournaments and classes omitting a family of pair-cancelling hypertournaments, together with the homogeneous cyclic order in arity three, are the only countably infinite homogeneous $n$-hypertournaments for $n\ge3$. We give some supporting evidence.

papers.title: A simplified temporal logic completeness proof
papers.abstract: A temporal logic discussed in the author's book "Logics of Time and Computation" is given a simpler proof of semantic completeness, eliminating some flaws in the original.

papers.title: Arithmetical Foundations - Recursion. Evaluation. Consistency
papers.abstract: We fix constructive foundations for Arithmetic on a map theoretical, algorithmic level. In contrast to elementhood and quantification based traditional foundations such as Principia Mathematica PM, Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory ZF, or v. Neumann-Goedel-Bernays set theory NGB, our fundamental primitive recursive theory PR has as its basic "undefined" (not further defined) terms just terms for objects and maps. Goodstein's axiomatic uniqueness rules are derived as theorems in PR - with equality definability as a side result -, S is obtained by predicate comprehension, and the equivalence of the theory of partially defined maps and the categorical theory of mu-recursion identifies mu-recursive maps and while-loops with partially defined maps. Keywords: Goedel theorems, primitive recursion, categorical free-variables Arithmetic, mu-recursion, totality

papers.title: Double negation stable h-propositions in cubical sets
papers.abstract: We give a construction of classifiers for double negation stable h-propositions in a variety of cubical set models of homotopy type theory and cubical type theory. This is used to give some relative consistency results: classifiers for double negation stable propositions exist in cubical sets whenever they exist in the metatheory; the Dedekind real numbers can be added to homotopy type theory without changing the consistency strength; we construct a model of homotopy type theory with extended Church's thesis, which states that all partial functions with double negation stable domain are computable.

papers.title: Pointwise provable equality and the failure of composition
papers.abstract: In their studies of pathologies in recursion categories, Montagna (1989) and Di Paola--Montagna (1991) introduce the algebraic systems $S'$ and $S'_T$, respectively, and claim that they are categories. We show that the proposed composition is not independent of the choice of representatives. For every consistent recursively enumerable extension $T$ of Peano arithmetic ($\mathrm{PA}$), we exhibit two unary programs whose partial functions are provably equal in $T$, separately at each standard input. Composing each after a program that searches for a $T$-proof of contradiction and returns its code yields programs that are not equivalent in this sense. An alternative proof uses the productivity of the complement of the diagonal halting set. Montagna's $S'$ is the case $T=\mathrm{PA}$. More generally, for consistent $T\supseteq\mathrm{PA}$, pointwise provable equality is a composition congruence exactly when $T$ proves every true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence, in which case it is extensional equality. This completeness condition fails for every consistent recursively enumerable $T\supseteq\mathrm{PA}$ by G\"odel's second incompleteness theorem. For every extension $T\supseteq\mathrm{PA}$, the least composition congruence containing pointwise provable equality is extensional equality if $T$ is $\Sigma^0_1$-sound and the universal relation otherwise.

papers.title: Maximality of the Do\v{s}en--Petri\'c Boolean Category
papers.abstract: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Adjoining any equation between parallel morphisms that does not follow from the defining equations, and closing under the operations on morphisms and uniform formula substitution, collapses this category to a preorder. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. The proof uses Boolean Coherence to select a pair of variable occurrences on which the two morphisms differ. Composition with morphisms selecting these occurrences, uniform substitution and two isomorphisms yield equality of the product projections. We prove that any zero-identity Boolean category satisfying such an additional equation under every interpretation of the variables is a preorder. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.

papers.title: Borel $(2n+1)$-coloring for bounded degree function graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G=(X,E)$ be a Borel graph generated by $n$-many bounded-to-one Borel functions. We show that $G$ admits a Borel proper $(2n+1)$-coloring, which answers a problem of Kechris, Solecki and Todor\v{c}evi\'{c}.

papers.title: Hilbert's Tenth problem and NP-completeness of Boolean Syllogistic with unordered cartesian product
papers.abstract: We relate the decidability problem for BS with unordered cartesian product with Hilbert's Tenth problem and prove that BS with unordered cartesian product is NP-complete.

papers.title: The set-theorist's real numbers
papers.abstract: Descriptive set theorists often refer to elements of the Baire space, $\mathcal{N} = {}^\omega\omega$, as ``reals.'' In this expository article, we present mathematical justification for this practice and highlight the advantages of working with $\mathcal{N}$ over $\mathbb{R}$ in the context of descriptive set theory.

papers.title: The norm formula in a Banach space and in its complete theory
papers.abstract: Let $h$ be the Hilbert norm on the real space $\ell_2(\mathbb{N})\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb{N})$, and put $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. For each of Bollob\'as's additive norms $h+\varepsilon q$, $\varepsilon>0$, and for the quadratic norm $\sqrt{h^2+q^2}$, the norm formula $\lVert x+y\rVert$ is unstable on the renormed space and has no independence property in its complete theory. We approximate $q(x+y)$ uniformly on bounded Hilbert balls by truncating small coordinates. For $n$ fixed test vectors and thresholds, the number of threshold patterns of $q(x+y)$ as $y$ varies is bounded by a polynomial in $n$ when the support sizes of the test vectors and of $y$ are bounded. These estimates give finite fat-shattering dimension for the translates of $q$ at every positive scale. The norm formula on a space can be stable, unstable without the independence property, or have the independence property. We give an example in each of these three cases where the formula has the independence property in the complete theory, and an example in each of the first two cases where it lacks that property in the complete theory. All five spaces satisfy a common midpoint estimate for uniform convexity, and each admits an isomorphism to Hilbert space of distortion at most $\sqrt3$.

papers.title: Relational Semantics and Completeness for Onto-Epistemic Logic
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a relational semantics for onto-epistemic logic with two semi-negations. The frames carry two pairs of quasi-orders and two commuting involutions. Some frames have nondistributive lattices of stable sets. The four- and nine-valued entailments are recovered as joint entailment on two particular finite frames. Sound and complete binary consequence calculi are given for both component entailments and for joint entailment. The joint Lindenbaum algebra embeds subdirectly into the product of its two component quotients. This embedding shows that joint derivability is the intersection of the two component derivability relations. The finite model property is proved using Dedekind-MacNeille completion and a filter-ideal representation of the resulting lattice. All three entailments are decidable by interleaving the search for a derivation with the search for a finite countermodel.

papers.title: The first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable
papers.abstract: We show that any ring of totally real abelian integers has a JR-number and therefore the first-order theory of every ring of totally real abelian integers is undecidable. It then follows that the first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable and that there is one formula without parameters defining $\Z$ in any such ring. The main arithmetic input is a recent paper of Bajpai, Das, Kedlaya, and Mello proving that the houses of cyclotomic integers form a well-ordered subset of $\R$.

papers.title: A note on distributive lattices with a commutative generalized implication
papers.abstract: We study distributive lattices with an ideal-valued generalized implication satisfying a commutativity identity. This class extends commutative weak Heyting algebras by allowing implication values to be non-principal ideals. We characterize its intersection with several known classes of gi-lattices, study gi-deductive systems and their relationship with gi-filters and gi-congruences, and extend the relational characterization of commutativity to this setting. The resulting correspondence yields a Priestley-style duality by restricting the established duality for gi-lattices.

papers.title: Chang's Omitting Types Theorem in Lukasiewicz Logic
papers.abstract: We prove Chang-style omitting types theorems for standard first-order Lukasiewicz logic. Starting from a prescribed model $M$, we obtain an extension that omits higher-complexity types while preserving lower-level types already realized in $M$. If $T$ is a $\Pi_{n+2}$-theory, every model of $T$ has an exact extension that preserves its realized $\Sigma_{n+1}$-types and omits every $\Sigma_{n+2}$-type not generated by a $\Sigma_{n+1}$-type. An iterated construction also omits infinity-universal types, whose unbounded quantifier complexity cannot eventually be generated by the corresponding lower-complexity fragments of a single type. The main tool is a refinement of Robinson's infinite forcing sensitive to the quantifier complexity of formulas.

papers.title: Determinateness in a classical theory of nonclassical truth
papers.abstract: Recent theories that take determinateness as primitive are either nonclassical theories of nonclassical truth, like Field's INT, or classical theories of classical truth, like Fujimoto and Halbach's CD and CD^+. This paper develops a third option: a classical theory of nonclassical truth. The theory, KFDcs, extends the Kripke-Feferman theory KFcs with a primitive determinateness predicate. Unlike CD^+, KFDcs keeps the iteration of truth unrestricted and gives up its completeness. With or without a consistency axiom, KFD is proof-theoretically equivalent to the theory \widehat{ID}_2 of twice iterated fixed points, with ordinal {\varphi}({\varphi}({\varepsilon}_0, 0)0), thus stronger than CD^+. It is also shown that replacing full induction with internal induction yields ordinal {\varphi}({\varphi}({\omega}, 0)0), and restricting internal induction to total formulae yields {\varphi}({\varepsilon_0},0), the ordinal of KF.

papers.title: The Contingent HOD Dichotomy
papers.abstract: The axiom V = HOD, referring to the class of hereditarily ordinal-definable sets, is contingently contingent by forcing---it holds contingently in the generic multiverse of some models of set theory but not others. Thus we introduce and investigate the \emph{contingent HOD dichotomy}, according to which either (1) the set-theoretic universe V is close to HOD by forcing---HOD is a ground, V = HOD is forceable, the universe is ordinal-definable from a set parameter $V=\text{HOD}_b$, the blurry HOD hierarchy collapses to kappa-HOD for some cardinal kappa, and furthermore these features are invariant by forcing and hold throughout the generic multiverse; or (2) the universe V is far from HOD by forcing in all those respects, so $V\neq\text{HOD}$, but also HOD is not a ground, V = HOD is not forceable, the set-theoretic universe is not ordinal-definable from a set, the universe is not kappa-HOD for any kappa, and these features hold invariantly throughout the generic multiverse. We investigate the nature of the dichotomy in connection with large cardinals, with set-theoretic geology, with the iterated $\text{HOD}^\alpha$ classes, and with the maximality principles MP and MP(R), showing generally that both prongs of the dichotomy occur with diverse set-theoretic phenomena.

papers.title: Frege's logic in Grundgesetze is nonclassical
papers.abstract: I show that the axioms and rules of inference about the horizontal in the subsystem of Grundgesetze without value-ranges fail to capture its intended interpretation. That is, I build a nonstandard model in which $-a$ is the true iff $a$ is not the false, thereby confirming a conjecture made by Landini that $a \to (-a) = a$ is not provable in this subsystem. This motivates our main result, namely, soundness and completeness proofs for the first-order fragment without value-ranges with respect to a new nonclassical semantics of boolean truncation. Simply put, the widespread assumption that Grundgesetze's first-order logic is classical first-order logic is mistaken.

papers.title: Strong Standard Completeness of a Hypersequent Calculus for Cyclic Involutive Residuated Lattices
papers.abstract: We present a hypersequent calculus $H_R$ for cyclic involutive residuated lattices and prove strong standard completeness for arbitrary theories in a fixed countable propositional language. Standard models are chains on $[0,1]$; neither commutativity nor equality of the monoid unit and the dualizing constant is assumed. The chain semantics is the class $K_R$ defined by unit cyclicity and all ordered finite-history conditions. Every countable member of $K_R$ embeds into a standard chain preserving the entire signature. The construction combines central-support reconstruction, gap insertion and relative contraction. A relative comparison construction supplies the required chain countermodels. We also prove admissibility of the unrestricted density rule for theoremhood and effective elimination from finite proofs without additional assumption leaves. Elimination uses terminating enumeration of density-free proofs; ordinary Cut is retained, and no complexity bound is claimed. Further constructions give bounded standard embeddings for nontrivial countable chains of involutive uninorm logic and pseudo-uninorm logic with weak commutativity. Using ordinary chain completeness for arbitrary theories, these yield strong standard completeness for both logics. A companion Lean~4 development formalizes the main results, with its scope and external inputs stated explicitly.

papers.title: A counterexample to the subgraphings approximate the cost problem
papers.abstract: We prove that for every $k\ge 2$, the free group $\mathbb{F}_k$ on $k$ generators admits a finite generating set $S$ such that the Schreier graphing of the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_k$ with respect to $S$ does not admit spanning subgraphings that would approximate the cost of the action. In particular, this gives an example of a graphing that spans a treeable countable pmp equivalence relation, but does not admit a spanning subtreeing.

papers.title: Borel combinatorics of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$-shift actions and hypersmooth equivalence relations
papers.abstract: We conjecture that for each integer $\ell\geq 2$, the equivalence relation arising from the shift action of $\mathbb{N}^{\ell}$ on $2^{\omega^{\ell}}$ is hypersmooth. We prove this conjecture for $\ell=2$, reduce the general case to a problem in Borel graph colorings, and establish the general case in measure. We also show that under certain mild hypotheses on a hypersmooth equivalence relation $E$, every finite-index Borel super-equivalence relation of $E$ is hypersmooth.

papers.title: On cover exacting cardinals
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Goldberg about cover exacting cardinals. Concretely, we show that if $\kappa$ is $\omega_1$-strongly compact, then no cardinal $\lambda>\kappa$ is $\gamma$-cover exacting for some cardinal $\gamma$.

papers.title: Exactly Proper Forcing
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of exact properness, a strong form of properness for uncountable models, and prove iteration theorems and the consistency of forcing axioms for this class. We discuss examples of posets in the class and give some applications of the forcing axioms.

papers.title: Melnikov residuals and stationary amalgamation in PAC fields
papers.abstract: We construct an invariant symmetric ternary relation with existence and stationarity over models for classes of characteristic-zero Frobenius fields associated with Melnikov formations. For proper formations, the automorphism theories of their canonical root-predicate expansions have amalgamation and no model companion. The underlying fields are then unbounded, and their theories are NSOP$_1$ but not simple. In this case, on triples of elementary submodels, the constructed relation implies ordinary nonforking, which implies Kim-independence, which implies linear disjointness; all three implications are strict. We also study p.e.c. fields with group actions, namely fields existentially closed in every regular extension carrying an extension of the action. We prove that the class of p.e.c.\ difference fields of characteristic zero is not elementary, and that the theory of all characteristic-zero difference fields with canonical root predicates has no model companion.

papers.title: Weak Generators in Stable Module Categories
papers.abstract: The aim of this note is to show that the existence of weak generators in the stable module category of a ring, or equivalently, of $p$-indigent modules in the terminology of Holston et al., depends on the underlying model of set theory.

papers.title: Non-Wellfounded and Labelled Sequent Calculi for Bimodal Provability Logics
papers.abstract: Bimodal provability logics are modal logics where the two modalities are interpreted as two formal provability predicates of arithmetic theories. We present modular labelled calculi for four different bimodal provability logics, whose rules arise from the relational semantics of these logics, while the second-order property of Noetherianity of models is enforced using techniques from cyclic proof theory. Completeness with respect to the semantics is established via proof search and countermodel construction. We further present regular and finite variants of the calculi via proof transformations.

papers.title: Approximating parametric suprema for constructible and power-constructible functions
papers.abstract: We prove that one may approximate parametric suprema of constructible and power-constructible functions using functions within the same class. This resolves a conjecture by Adiceam and Cluckers, which was posited after studying a question posed by Sarnak. We apply our result to prove that a certain subclass of Cexp-class distributions is tempered and to make uniform a bound concerning pushforward measures.

papers.title: The geometry of Coherent topoi and Ultrastructures
papers.abstract: We show that coherent topoi are right Kan injective with respect to flat embeddings of topoi. We recover the ultrastructure on their category of points as a consequence of this result. We speculate on possible notions of ultracategory in various arenas of formal model theory.

papers.title: On Some Infinitary Logics
papers.abstract: We define a new class of infinitary logics $\mathscr L^1_{\kappa,\alpha}$ generalizing Shelah's logic $\mathbb L^1_\kappa$ defined in \cite{MR2869022}. If $\kappa=\beth_\kappa$ and $\alpha <\kappa$ is infinite then our logic coincides with $\mathbb L^1_\kappa$. We study the relation between these logics for different parameters $\kappa$ and $\alpha$. We give many examples of classes of structures that can or cannot be defined in these logics. Finally, we give a different version of Lindstr\"{o}m's Theorem for $\mathbb L^1_\kappa$ in terms of the $\phi$-submodel relation.

papers.title: On the optimality of the HOD dichotomy
papers.abstract: In the first part of the manuscript, we establish several consistency results concerning Woodin's HOD hypothesis and large cardinals around the level of extendibility. First, we prove that the first extendible cardinal can be the first strongly compact in HOD. Second, answering a question in \cite{CFH}, we prove that the first supercompact cardinal can be the first strongly compact, non supercompact, of HOD. We extend a former result of Woodin by showing that under the HOD hypothesis the first extendible cardinal is $C^{(1)}$-supercompact in HOD. We also show that the first cardinal-correct extendible may not be extendible, thus answering a question by Gitman and Osinski \cite[\S9]{GitOsi}. In the second part of the manuscript, we discuss the extent to which weak covering can fail below the first supercompact cardinal $\delta$ in a context where the HOD hypothesis holds. Answering a question of Cummings et al. \cite{CumFriGol}, we show that under the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis there are many singulars $\kappa<\delta$ where $\mathrm{cf}^{\mathrm{HOD}}(\kappa)=\mathrm{cf}(\kappa)$ and $\kappa^{+\mathrm{HOD}}=\kappa^{+}.$ In contrast, we also show that the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis is consistent with $\delta$ carrying a club of $\mathrm{HOD}$-regulars cardinals $\kappa$ such that $\kappa^{+\mathrm{HOD}}<\kappa^{+}$. Finally, we close the manuscript with a discussion about the $\mathrm{HOD}$ hypothesis and $\omega$-strong measurability.
